cities.base: Old town, walkable to Mount Phousi and the night market
cities.name: Luang Prabang

cities.base: Riverside bungalow strip, near the bike rental shops and balloon launch site
cities.name: Vang Vieng

places.name: Luang Prabang Night Market
places.note: Good for food stalls, skip most of the souvenir tables since they're identical to the last five towns.

places.name: Kuang Si Falls
places.note: Entry 60,000 LAK (July 2026), open 08:00 to 17:30, with the Free the Bears centre inside the gate and swimming in the tiered pools below the cascade. Arrive before 10am or it is a tour-bus swimming pool by noon.

places.name: Pak Ou Caves
places.note: Two caves where the Nam Ou meets the Mekong: Tham Ting, full of Buddha statues left by pilgrims, and Tham Phum up a steep stair, dark, so bring a light. Entry 20,000 LAK; the boat is the 30 dollar part, and the ride is the point.

places.name: Blue Lagoon / Tham Phu Kham
places.note: Blue Lagoon 1 at Tham Phu Kham, open 08:30 to 17:30, entry 10,000 LAK. Packed with tour groups by 11am, so be there at opening or find a quieter swimming spot nearby.

places.name: Countryside cycling loop
places.note: Roads get rough after rain, better in dry season or rent an e-bike.

places.name: Royal Palace Museum (Haw Kham)
places.note: The former royal residence, and the context for everything else in town in about 75 minutes. Open daily 08:00 to 11:30 and 13:30 to 15:30 per Wanderlog (an older listing gave Tuesdays off, so check); 60,000 LAK, bags and shoes off, no photos inside.

places.name: Wat Xieng Thong
places.note: The most important temple in the city, with the mosaic tree-of-life wall and the gilded funeral chapel. Open daily 06:00 to 18:00, entry 30,000 LAK; quiet before 9am, tour groups arrive after.

places.name: Alms Giving Ceremony (Tak Bat), Sakkaline Road
places.note: Monks file out at dawn to collect rice. Worth seeing once but the crowd of tourists shoving cameras in monks' faces is genuinely uncomfortable. Buy sticky rice from a proper vendor if you join in, not the plastic-stool sellers who prep it in advance.

places.name: Luang Prabang Morning Market (Phousi Market)
places.note: Produce, river weed and jungle food, not staged for visitors like the night market, open 05:00 to 12:00. Not for the squeamish: live and freshly killed animals are part of daily commerce here.

places.name: Tamarind Restaurant
places.note: Lao tasting platters, jeow dips and sausages, done properly and explained rather than guessed at. Lunch 11:00 to 16:15 and dinner 17:30 to 21:30, closed Sundays.

places.name: Bamboo Bridge over the Nam Khan
places.note: Rebuilt by hand each dry season and taken down before the floods, so it should be up from about November; Wanderlog lists it closed, so check. Toll 7,000 LAK, a quiet stretch of the Nam Khan away from the main strip.

places.name: Nam Song River bank (Riverside strip)
places.note: Free walk along the river with the karst wall backdrop, best right before sunset. Bars along here get loud after dark if that's not what you want.

places.name: Tham Chang Cave
places.note: Steep short climb to a lit cave with a view over town and the karsts, open 08:00 to 18:00. Wanderlog lists entry as free, but check the price at the gate; a good rainy-day backup since most of it is covered.
places.neighborhood: South of town, across the river

places.name: Vang Vieng Organic Farm
places.note: The Organic Farm restaurant north of town: goat cheese, mulberry wine and mojitos and simple Lao food on a working farm, 08:00 to 17:00 daily. A natural stop mid cycling loop rather than a destination on its own.

places.name: Vang Vieng Night Market
places.note: Smaller and less polished than Luang Prabang's, mostly food stalls and a few clothing stands. Good cheap dinner option, nothing to plan a whole evening around.

places.name: Riverside Restaurants near the old bridge
places.note: Cluster of open-air restaurants facing the karsts across the river, good sunset dinner spot. Food is average tourist-Lao, you're paying for the view.
places.neighborhood: Riverside, near the old bamboo bridge

places.name: Balloon launch field (north of town)
places.note: The launch field in the rice paddies north of town, where the sunrise balloons go up. Weather cancels flights more often than you'd like, so keep the morning flexible.

places.name: Kuang Si Falls main cascade
places.note: The tall multi-tier waterfall you see on every postcard, reached by a short uphill path past the pools. Best photographed before the light gets harsh and before the crowds walking up from the lower pools arrive.

places.name: Free the Bears rescue centre
places.note: Sanctuary for Asiatic moon bears rescued from bile farms and traps, inside the park entrance and free with the Kuang Si ticket, 08:00 to 17:00. Shaded enclosures, worth ten minutes on the way in.

places.name: Ban Ou Cave village noodle stalls
places.note: Simple roadside noodle and grilled skewer stalls that tuk-tuks often stop at on the way back from the falls. Nothing fancy, cheap and fast, useful if you skipped breakfast to beat the crowds.

places.name: Elephant riding camps near Kuang Si
places.note: Several outfits along the road offer elephant rides or bathing sessions. Animal welfare standards are inconsistent and several documented cases of poor treatment exist in the area. Skip unless you've personally vetted a specific sanctuary.

places.name: Ban Xang Hai (Whisky Village)
places.note: Standard stop on the way upriver, rice whisky distilling in clay jars and a strip of stalls selling it in snake-infused bottles. Feels staged and every boat stops here, worth ten minutes not thirty.

places.name: Ban Xang Khong weaving and paper village
places.note: Riverside village near Luang Prabang doing saa paper and traditional weaving, a reasonable detour if the boat operator includes it or you have spare time before departure, not directly on the Pak Ou run.

places.name: Riverside noodle stalls near the Pak Ou landing
places.note: Simple noodle soup and grilled snacks from small family stalls by the boat dock, nothing fancy, useful if you time the return trip around lunch instead of eating back in town.

places.name: Elephant camps near Pak Ou
places.note: Several riverside camps pitch elephant rides and bathing add-ons to the boat trip. Animal welfare standards at these operations are inconsistent at best, skip and keep the day to the river and caves.

places.name: Tham Phu Kham Cave
places.note: Steep 10 to 15 minute climb from the lagoon to the cave mouth, slippery and unlit, with a reclining Buddha just inside. The cave is free and a headlamp rents for 10,000 LAK; the valley view from the entrance is the real payoff.

places.name: Blue Lagoon swimming area
places.note: The turquoise pool everyone comes for, with a rope swing and a tree platform for jumping in. Genuinely striking water color, also genuinely packed with tour buses and day-trippers by mid-morning. Go at opening or accept the crowd.

places.name: Nam Xay Viewpoint
places.note: Steep, rope-assisted scramble, 45 to 60 minutes up, to one of the best karst panoramas around Vang Vieng. Open 05:00 to 17:30, about 20,000 LAK; go early, there is almost no shade.

places.name: Blue Lagoon 2
places.note: A quieter alternative to the original lagoon, roughly 15km further out on rougher roads. Fewer tour groups, still has a swing and clear water, worth it if the crowds at the main site put you off.

places.name: Elephant Cave (Tham Xang)
places.note: Named for a rock formation resembling an elephant near the entrance. Smaller and less dramatic than Tham Phu Kham, skippable if you only have half a day and already did the main lagoon.

places.name: Tham Nam (Water Cave) tubing
places.note: You pull yourself through the flooded cave on an inner tube via a fixed rope, headlamp required and usually rented on site. Fun for 20 minutes, murky water, not for anyone with mild claustrophobia.

places.name: Blue Lagoon entrance souvenir stalls
places.note: Skip. A row of identical stalls selling the same sarongs and snacks as everywhere else in Vang Vieng, no reason to linger here specifically.

places.name: Khaiphaen
places.note: Lao kitchen opposite Wat Choum Khong, open since 2015 and rated 4.7 from about 1,200 Google reviews. Order the red curry chicken, Luang Prabang sausage and or lam; about 100,000 LAK a head on the 2023 menu, so expect a little more. Closed Sundays.
places.neighborhood: Ban Wat Nong, opposite Wat Choum Khong

places.name: 3 Nagas Restaurant
places.note: The restaurant of the 3 Nagas heritage hotel: larb, Luang Prabang salad and or lam, mains 9 to 13 dollars with service and tax included (Sept 2025 menu). The 27 dollar Lao set is the order for one big dinner.

places.name: Atsalin Restaurant
places.note: Cheap Lao cooking from a kitchen at the street front, dishes from about 20,000 LAK each (Jan 2024 price), so order two or three. Closed Sundays.

places.name: Nisha Restaurant Indian Halal Food
places.note: Halal Indian with plenty for vegetarians; aloo mutter, garlic naan and a large Beer Lao came to 34,000 LAK in Jan 2024. The night off from sticky rice, not a reason to come to Laos.
places.neighborhood: King Kit Salad Road, Ban Aham

places.name: Wat Wisunarat (Wat Visoun)
places.note: Built 1512 to 1513 and rebuilt 1896 to 1898, in the oldest temple style in Laos. The grounds are free; the main building costs 20,000 LAK (Fodor's says 30,000), and Wat Aham is next door.

places.name: Wat May Souvannapoumaram (Wat Mai)
places.note: Built in 1780 and restored 1817 to 1836, right beside the Royal Palace, so do the two in one morning. Entry 30,000 LAK; the dawn alms round passes close by.
places.neighborhood: Sisavangvong Road, beside the Royal Palace

places.name: Traditional Arts and Ethnology Centre
places.note: The best short introduction to the ethnic groups of Laos, in a small museum behind Dara Market. Entry 35,000 LAK, allow 75 minutes, closed Mondays.

places.name: UXO Lao Visitor Centre
places.note: Unexploded ordnance exhibits and a film on the bombs still in Lao fields, behind the Souphanouvong monument. Free, donations welcome; the tourism office says daily 08:00 to 16:00, though one listing shows a 12:00 to 13:00 break, so check.
places.neighborhood: Ban Naviengkham, south of the old town

places.name: Heuan Chan Heritage House
places.note: A pre-colonial wooden house kept as a museum, down an alley off Sisavangvong Road. Adult entry about 2.23 dollars, open 09:00 to 17:00, and 45 minutes is enough.

places.name: Phousi Hill (Mount Phousi)
places.note: The 100 m hill in the middle of the old town, with temples halfway up and on the summit. Ticket 30,000 LAK (May 2026); hours vary, check, as one listing gives 08:00 to 16:30 and another 06:00 to 18:00, and the sunset crowd is heavy.

places.name: Ock Pop Tok Living Craft Centre
places.note: Weaving centre on the Mekong with the Silk Road Kitchen cafe on site, open 08:00 to 20:00. Entry was free on an older listing, so check the price, and stay for a drink by the river.

places.name: Wat Aham
places.note: Probably early 19th century, a quiet monastery right beside Wat Visoun and far less visited. Free to enter; hours vary, check.

places.name: Wat Sensoukharam
places.note: Old-town temple on the Mekong side of the peninsula, an easy stop on the walk from the Royal Palace to Wat Xieng Thong. Free to enter; hours vary, check.

places.name: Green Restaurant
places.note: Riverside near the bamboo bridge and open 06:30 to 23:00, so it covers breakfast through a late dinner. A stir-fry with rice is about 3.20 dollars (2026); busy in the evening, calmer in the afternoon.

places.name: Vela Cafe and Restaurant
places.note: Cafe on the main road; the breakfast set with coffee, tea or a smoothie starts at 3 dollars (2026). It shuts 14:30 to 18:00 for the afternoon and all day Monday.

places.name: Vang Vieng Morning Market
places.note: The town's own market, a short ride north of the centre, open 06:00 to 17:00 and free to walk round. Go early, before the lagoon day trips take over the morning.

places.name: Pha Ngern View Point
places.note: Karst viewpoint west of town, entry about 20,000 LAK, allow two hours. An October 2025 visitor found the trail abandoned, so ask in town before you go; hours vary, check.

places.name: Kaeng Nyui Waterfall
places.note: Waterfall northeast of town with an informal fee of about 33,000 LAK (one visitor in Dec 2024 was asked 100,000). Signs at the site suggested a temporary closure, so check it is open before you ride out.

outings.why: Turquoise pools and a waterfall, but a tour-bus swimming pool by noon so go before 10am.
outings.name: Kuang Si Falls
outings.season: year-round, road turns rough in wet season

outings.why: The caves are minor, the two hours cruising the Mekong to get there is the actual point.
outings.name: Pak Ou Caves boat trip

outings.why: A 45 minute climb then a crowded but worthwhile sunset over the town.
outings.name: Mount Phousi sunset climb

outings.why: Photogenic karst swimming hole, packed with tour groups by 11am so go early or find a quieter spot nearby.
outings.name: Blue Lagoon / Tham Phu Kham

outings.why: An hour aloft over the karsts at dawn, but weather cancels it more often than you'd like so keep the morning flexible.
outings.name: Vang Vieng sunrise balloon flight
outings.fallback: Sleep in and start the cycling loop earlier instead.

outings.why: A half-day loop through rice fields and villages, rough after rain so better in dry season or on an e-bike.
outings.name: Vang Vieng countryside cycling loop
outings.fallback: Rent an e-bike instead of a regular bike if roads are wet.

destination.name: Laos (Luang Prabang & Vang Vieng)
destination.pitch: Slow river towns, waterfalls, and karst countryside — but the flights alone eat two of your seven days.
destination.caveat: No nonstop from the US exists, so you'll burn close to two full days in transit each way for six nights on the ground. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.food: Night market food stalls and noodle soup breakfasts run $2-5 a plate.
because.nature: Kuang Si Falls, the Mekong boat ride, and the Blue Lagoon karst scenery.
because.culture: Pak Ou Caves and Luang Prabang's temples and night market carry the old Lao capital feel.
because.adventure: Sunrise ballooning and countryside cycling around Vang Vieng's karst hills.
because.relaxation: Slow riverside towns with no real urgency once the day's outing is done.
